findings.title: async forEach makes the surrounding try/catch dead and deletions fire-and-forget
findings.body: The change turns `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach((bookingRef) => {...})` into `forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` so `getCalendar` can be awaited. Because `forEach` never awaits async callbacks, (1) the surrounding `try/catch` (lines 124-139) can no longer catch any error thrown after the first await — a failed dynamic import or a rejected `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` now escapes as an unhandled promise rejection, which on Node's default settings can terminate the server process; (2) the function proceeds to `sendRequestRescheduleEmail` and `return true` without waiting for the calendar/video deletions, so on serverless the response may complete (and the function be frozen) before the old events are removed, leaving stale events on attendees' calendars. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` and keep the try/catch around it.

findings.title: async forEach makes the surrounding try/catch dead and deletions fire-and-forget
findings.body: Identical to the vital app: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` was introduced to await the now-async `getCalendar`. `forEach` does not await async callbacks, so the `try/catch` around it (lines 124-139) is now dead code for anything that happens after the first `await`, and any rejection from `getCalendar`, `calendar.deleteEvent`, or `deleteMeeting` becomes an unhandled promise rejection. Additionally the reschedule email is sent and `true` returned before the deletions finish, so a failed or incomplete cleanup is silently ignored. Replace with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))`.

findings.title: requestReschedule deletes calendar/video events in an un-awaited async forEach
findings.body: In the `requestReschedule` mutation, `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` now awaits `getCalendar` inside the callback. `forEach` does not wait for async callbacks, so the mutation sends the reschedule email, fires the BOOKING_CANCELLED webhooks, and returns while the calendar event deletions (`calendar.deleteEvent`) and video deletions (`deleteMeeting`) may still be in flight — and any failure (e.g. the dynamic import rejecting) surfaces as an unhandled promise rejection with no logging or error handling at all, since there is no try/catch here. Previously at least `getCalendar` was synchronous so its errors propagated to the caller. Collect the promises and `await Promise.all(...)` (ideally with per-item error handling) before returning.

findings.title: Dynamic imports are evaluated eagerly, so all app bundles still load at startup
findings.body: The object literal `const appStore = { applecalendar: import("./applecalendar"), ... }` evaluates every `import()` call as soon as `@calcom/app-store` itself is imported, so all ~28 app chunks begin loading immediately for any process that touches this module — the same startup cost as the previous static imports, just with extra microtask hops. If the intent of the PR is to defer loading apps until they are actually used, this does not achieve it; the values should be thunks, e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, with call sites invoking the function. As written the change adds async complexity to every consumer without the advertised loading benefit.
